alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 9:42PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From Sunday morning through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
ESFGJT

Low pressure begins to dig southward from the PACNW on Friday,
tapping into a fetch of Pacific moisture that will evolve into an
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest this weekend.
Showers and thunderstorms develop on Friday and Saturday across the
region. Lighter rainfall totals Friday and Saturday will reflect,
initially lower, moisture. However, a few thunderstorms could produce
impactful downpours on saturated soils left over from last weekend's
historic rainfall.

Deeper moisture develops Saturday night and early Sunday. This is
expected to produce heavier and more widespread rainfall across
southeast UT and southwest CO Sunday and Monday, mostly below 10000
feet. While rivers are forecast to remain below action stage, a
growing concern lies in the potential for runoff around saturated
hillsides in the region. This could produce rock, mud, and debris
flows onto roadways, as well as flash flood prone burn scars, washes,
slot canyons, and arroyos. Early estimates predict an area of 1 to 2
inches of new rainfall for portions of southeast UT and southwest CO.

This is a preliminary forecast that hinges on slight shifts in a
strong moisture plume impacting the region. It also attempts to
capture the most statistically likely outcome, despite stronger and
weaker outlier predictions. Outdoor enthusiasts, motorists, and
residents of recent flood impacted areas are encouraged to remain
abreast of the developing forecast in the coming days.

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147606
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 31, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 31, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 31, 7:00AM - October 31, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
